title: A local ring is henselian (idempotent lifting) iff simple roots of monic polynomials lift
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a local ring. The following are equivalent: (i) $R$ is henselian in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], i.e. for every finite $R$-algebra $B$ every idempotent of $B/\mathfrak mB$ lifts uniquely to an idempotent of $B$; (ii) for every monic polynomial $f\in R[T]$ and every $a_0\in\kappa$ with $\overline f(a_0)=0$ and $\overline{f'}(a_0)\neq0$ (where $\overline f\in\kappa[T]$ is the reduction of $f$) there exists $a\in R$ with $f(a)=0$ and $a\bmod\mathfrak m=a_0$.

source.place: algebra.tex Definition Tag 04GE (definition-henselian: (ii) is Stacks' definition of a henselian local ring) and Lemma Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), (1)<=>(10) (every finite R-algebra is a finite product of local rings); more-algebra.tex Definition Tag 09XE (definition-henselian-pair) with the remark following it (for a local ring, (R,m) is a henselian pair iff R is henselian) and Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair), (1)<=>(3) (idempotents of B/IB lift uniquely for finite B)
